main_text.head: PRÆLECTIO SECUNDA
In quâ ostenditur, non esse in Bonæ Intentionis conscientiâ satis præ-sidii, ut in eâ possit aliquis tutò acquiescere.
ROM. III. 8.

p.i: Et non sicut blasphemamur, & sicut quidam aiunt nos dicere, Faciamus mala, ut eve-niant bona : quorum damnatio justa est.

main_text.p: Mentem humanam aliquid in se Divini continere magno consensu fassi sunt veterum Sapientes: qui eam Divinae particulam aurae ² Διὸς [?] ἀπαύγασμα [?] ἢ ἀπόσπασμα [?], decerptósque ab Diis immortalibus animos nostros & quasi delibatos, Dixerunt. Quin & altius ipsorum nonnulli surgentes, & audacius prolocuti, Mentem Deum ipsum dicere, eique velut Deo ³ templa exigere, non sunt veriti. ⁴ ʻO νοῦς γὰρ ἡμῶν ὁ θεὸς [?], inquit, apud Plutarchum, Menander: & Ovidius ⁵Mens quoque numen habet: & Seneca, ⁶ Quid aliud mens [?] animum, quàm Deum in humano corpore ¹ Horat.
Epist. 13. ψυχὴ ἑκάστου δαίμων [?]. Xenoph. apud Aristot. 2. T.p. 6.

page.notes: The title line "In quâ ostenditur..." is set larger than the text and is treated as a heading. The running head is faint; its reading "De Bona Intentione" is uncertain. The verse is printed in italic throughout. Right margin notes, in order: "¹ Horat."; "² Satyr. 2."; "³ Epist."; "Menti ades in Capitolio, vid. Cic. 2 de nat. Deor. & Liv. lib. 23."; "⁴ Plutarch. in quaest. Platon."; "⁵ Ovid. Fast."; "⁶ Senec." These are set beside the lines of the text and are shown here by their marks as far as they can be read. The marks on the Greek lines and the mark placed before "Mentem" are not clear enough to be certain. The handwritten word at the foot right ("hos.") is not printed and is left out. The Greek on line 1 and in the foot line is only approximately read.
